lawyer:
Md Moniruzzaman (Rubel) Deputy Attorney-General with Abul Kalam Azad Khan with Abdur Rokib and Marufa Akhter, Assistant Attorney-Generals ---------- For the State. 
Mansurul Hoque Chowdhury Senior Advocate with Subrata Saha Advocate -------- For Appellant in Cr Appeal 7675 of 2012.

parties:
State  ---------
VS
Md Nazimuzzaman Yon and another -------- Condemned-Prisoners
full_judgment:
59. In cross-examination PW 33 denied the defence suggestion that Raju was actually arrested on 24-2-2011 and was in illegal custody for two days. He also denied that Raju was physically and mentally tortured in custody. He inquired into the age of accused Raju, but did not collect any documentary evidence regarding his age. 

 61. After closing the prosecution evidence, accused were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure wherein they reiterated their innocence, but did not examine any witness in their defence. They, however, submitted two statements explaining their condition in custody and under what circumstances they made their confessions. In the statement made by accused Yon, he stated that the police arrested him at 2-00 o'clock in the night following 31-1-2011 from his rented house at Savar and without giving him any opportunity to explain anything just took him to the DB office and started torturing. The police electrocuted him and beat him keeping his legs upward. As he declined to make any confession, he was further tortured to which he became sick. To avoid further torture he was compelled to make confession before media. Thereafter, police gave him a written script and asked him to memorize it. They threatened him of crossfire and also of implicating his mother and cousin in this case. Under the circumstances he was compelled to make confession before the Magistrate. He knew nothing about the murder of his maternal uncle. In the written statement made by accused Raju he took similar defence that on unbearable and inhuman torture he was compelled to make confession. In addition, he stated that police took him in a vacant place, made some blank fires and threatened him of killing if he did not make the confession. They made a script and asked him to memorize it and make confession accordingly before the Magistrate. He was produced before the Magistrate for making confession one day before expiry of his remand with a threat that if he did not make confession he would be taken back for remaining one day and would be further tortured. Actually the real culprit was allowed to go scot-free and the DB falsely victimized him. He further stated that he had passed SSC examination from German Technical Training Centre in 2010 and was the only son of his parents. 

 63. Mr Md Moniruzaman, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State submits that the accused persons themselves made confessions before the Metropolitan Magistrate, which were inculpatory in nature, true and voluntary. Those were recorded in strict compliance with the procedure as provided in law. Besides, there were other convincing and credible evidences, namely, recovery of incriminating articles, DNA test reports and postmortem reports, which fully corroborate the confessions. The confessions were proved by PW 18 Keshab Roy Chowdhury, the recording Magistrate, postmortem reports by PW 27 Dr AKM Shofiuzzaman, DNA test reports by PW 28 Pilu Momtaz and recovery of incriminating articles by number of local witnesses, namely, PWs 10-17, 20, 22-23, 30 and also by the Investigating Officer PW 33. Accused Yon in his confession gave a believable description of the occurrence and also disclosed the motive, which appears to be very natural. The name of co-accused Raju was disclosed in his confession and he (Raju) was subsequently arrested from Phultala, Khulna on 25-2-2011. On that very day he was brought to Dhaka and some incriminating articles were recovered at his instance. 

 64. In the postmortem reports, the injuries were mentioned to be antemortem and homicidal. The manner of occurrence as appears in the confessions clearly matches the postmortem reports as well as the evidence of the doctor. In such a position there is no minimum doubt that the accused were involved in the murders. Learned trial Judge on considering evidence and other materials on record rightly convicted them. 

 67. Mr Chowdhury further submits that the evidence PW 19 Ramij Member, landlord of accused Yon proves that he was arrested in the dead of night following 31-1-2011. If he was arrested in the midnight following 31-1-2011, the question of recovery of the knives from the drain adjacent to DIT Extension Road, black jeans pant and currency notes from Savar in the afternoon on 31-1-2011 did not arise. All these anomalies and contradictions make the case doubtful and indicate that some other persons were actually involved in the killing, who were in conflict with the victims or in a motive to grab their property. The police under influence of the original culprits made the two minor boys scapegoats and victimized them. 

 68. Mr Chowdhury then submits that in their confessions the accused were shown to have cleaned the knives and gloves after commission of the occurrence, but the gloves were found blood stained at the time of recovery. On the other hand the knives were recovered from a muddy drain, but found dry and clean. It clearly indicates that the knives and gloves were actually not recovered, but brought by police just to show recovery in corroboration of their confessions. It is also difficult to believe that when they cleaned their knives and gloves just after the occurrence presumably for screening out the evidence, they would keep the blood stained jeans pant hanging on a rope to be recovered by police and used by the prosecution as an evidence against them. If two persons are slaughtered in an apartment building, their groaning sounds must be heard by other inhabitants, but no such evidence is there. 

 69. Mr Chowdhury referring to the evidence of PWs 16, 19 and 33 further submits that the black jeans allegedly recovered from the house of Yon was actually not the pant which was produced in the Court and sent for DNA test. Its length and waist as mentioned in the seizure list did not match the pant. In such a position there is every possibility that the police using their power victimized the innocent boys and collected evidence to get them punished. If the evidences of the seizure list witnesses are critically sifted, it would be further established that in recovery and seizure of those articles, which have been used to corroborate their confessions, were not seized following the procedural law specifically section 103 of the Code. So, the so-called recovery of some planted articles cannot be used to corroborate the confessions of the accused. 

 72. Mr Khasru refers to the postmortem reports and submits that the injuries were made by heavily sharp cutting weapons, but the two knives which were used for domestic purpose in cutting vegetable were never so heavy. Therefore, recovery of the two knives actually did not corroborate the confessions to that extent. There was also contradiction between the evidences of PWs 22 and 23 in respect of manner of recovery as to whether the accused was there and showed the materials to be recovered. 

 74. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and gone through the evidence and other materials on record including the confessions, seizure lists, evidences of the local seizure list witnesses, DNA test and autopsy reports. There is no dispute over the fact that the victims were killed at their rented flat at 77, Naya Paltan (1st floor) sometime within 23-00 hours on 27-1-2011 to 12-00 hours on 28-1-2011. PW 2 Jamil Ahmed Khan Ripan first noticed that the flat was locked from outside, when he along with his wife and mother went there at 12-00 hours on 28-1-2011 to attend an invitation. His mother informed it to the informant, who communicated the police at Paltan Model Police Station. A Sub-Inspector of Police named Nasir Uddin (PW 29), informant Md Abdus Samad Khan (PW 1), victims family friend Md Hasan (PW 4), landlord Harunur Rashid (PW 5), an inmate of the apartment building named Minhaz Rashid (PW 6), one of the victims relations Humayun Kabir Khan (PW 8) first entered into the flat breaking the lock and saw the dead bodies in the master bedroom of the flat. From their evidences it comes out that they were slaughtered to death, the households were scattered, dead body of victim Rahima Khanam was lying on the bed and that of Farhad Khan was on the floor. 

 76. It appears from the evidence of PW 33 that accused Raju was arrested from Phultala, Khulna on 25-2-2011 at 10-10 am. He was brought to Dhaka on the same day and seven EURO coins and a guitar were recovered from his house at Savar at 16-40 hours. Thereafter, some other incriminating articles, namely, two pairs of gloves and some gold ornaments were also recovered from different places in Dhaka at his instance. After the recovery, he was produced before the Metropolitan Magistrate on 26-2-2011 and was taken on remand for 3 (three) days. On expiry of the said period, he was produced back to the Magistrate on 1-3-2011 and made confession under section 164 of the Code. Learned Magistrate deposed in support of the confession and formally proved it in evidence, which appears to be true and voluntary. 

 79. In the above quoted confessions, both the accused involved themselves in commission of the occurrence and gave believable description of the same. Recovery of the incriminating articles, namely, black jeans pant and currency notes from the rented house of Yon at his instance, phone set of victim Farhad Khan from the house of Raju, gold ornaments from Ma Joya Jewelers at Mirpur, and the gloves slightly stained with blood from the sun shed of an adjacent house at the instance of accused Raju, and that from the jewelry shop of Subodh Ghosh (PW 20) on 31-1-2011, two DNA test reports and autopsy report, seizure lists and evidences of the local seizure list witnesses except PW 19 fully corroborate the confessions. 

 84. PW 33 Md Abu-al Khayer, 2nd IO of the case who submitted the charge sheet stated that on the basis of intelligence information (presumably the can lists of Farhad Khan collected by the 1st 10, which are available in record but not adduced in evidence) he had arrested accused Nazimuzzaman Yon on 31-1-2011 from Mipur Mazar Road. Nowhere in record, it is specifically mentioned at what point of time he was arrested. Some seizure figs all dated 31-1-2011 were proved and exhibited: Of them exhibit-9 shows that a black jeans pant, navy blue hoody, seven currency notes, each of Taka 1000 were recovered from the rented house of Yon at Savar on 31-1-2011 at 16-40 hours at his showing. This recovery was proved by two local seizure list witnesses named Md Khalil (PW 16) and Kabir Osman Suman (PW 17) as well as by PW 33 himself, who was the seizing Police Officer and 10 of the case. Two currency notes of Taka 500 each were recovered and seized at 17-10 hours on the same day under a seizure list (exhibit-25) from PW 19 Md Ramij Uddin, landlord of Yon. This seizure list was proved by a local seizure list witness named Md Mobhar Ali (PW 30) as well as by PW 33 himself. PW 19 Md Ramij Uddin, stated that Yon was his tenant and arrested at about 2-00/2-30 in the night following 31-1-2011 and no money was recovered from him or no seizure list was prepared showing that recovery. But he did not dispute the authenticity of his signature put on the seizure list, rather admitted it by saying that he put the signature sitting at the DB office. The seizure list witnesses, namely, PWs 16, 17, 30, and 33 were exhaustively cross-examined, but disclosed nothing adverse about the time of recovery of those articles. The defence also did not challenge the time of recovery by putting contrary suggestions while cross-examined them. Accused Yon in his confession clearly stated that police had arrested him from the front of. Shah Ali Mazar, Mirpur at midday on 31-1-2011. Under the facts and circumstances it can easily be understood that PW 19 was obliged to his tenant and did not tell the truth while deposed. It is, therefore, not correct to say that the recovery was made before his arrest. 

 85. Some other articles, namely, a gold chain, earring with pendant and ring were recovered from a jewelry shop at Bara Bazar on 31-1-2011 at 20-15 hours. This recovery was proved by the evidence of PW 20 Subodh Ghosh, owner of the jewelry shop and that of PW 33 Md Abu-al Khayer read with exhibit-13 (seizure list) and material exhibits-IX series (seized ornaments). 

 86. Another set of ornaments, namely, two earrings and nose pins were recovered from a jewelry shop at Mirpur on 25-2-2011 at 15-30 hours. This recovery was proved by the evidence of PW 13 Jiban Sarker, owner of the jewelry shop, and that of PW 14 Motaleb Kha, a local seizure list witness read with exhibit-8 and material exhibits-V series. 

 87. Two knives wrapped with newspaper were recovered from a drain adjacent to DIT Extension Road on 31-1-2011 at 23-10 hours at the instance of accused Yon. This recovery was proved by PWs 22, 23 and 33 read with exhibit-17 and material exhibit-IX series. PW 22 Md Bashir Uddin proved the seizure list and his signature there. He also proved the seized knives as material exhibits stating that there was no dirt or blood stain on those knives. PW 23 Md Abdul Hannan stated that there was dirt on the newspaper only. Both the said seizure list witnesses were apparently independent, and we do not find any reason to disbelieve their evidences. Cleaning of the knives, wrapping with newspaper and throwing into a nearby drain were mentioned in confessions of both the accused. 

 90. The autopsy reports show cut-throat injuries and incised wounds on the left side of their neck/lower neck. PW 27 Dr AKM Sofiuzzaman proved the autopsy reports in evidence and stated that those injuries were ante-mortem and homicidal in nature and caused death .to the victims. In cross-examination he made it clear that those injuries could not be self-made. 

 91. Learned Advocates for the defence also assail the evidentiary value of the recoveries on the ground of non-compliance with the provisions of section 103 of the Code. The object of this provision of law is to conduct a search fairly and also to ensure that no articles are planted by police. In the present case recoveries were made in presence of local witnesses and occupants of the places of recovery and they deposed supporting the recovery except PW 19. It is also to be kept in mind that a search on secret information of police as a routine work, and recovery of articles following information by an accused under police custody as described in section 27 of the Evidence Act are not exactly same. Even in a simple search, presence of two respectable inhabitants of the area and occupants of the place searched may not be possible. The Court should not take a rigid view regarding compliance of section 103 of the Code in each and every case. 

 92. Let us examine the age of the accused-appellants and consider the submissions of their learned Advocates that they were children at the time of occurrence. The Metropolitan Magistrate allowed an application filed by the 10 for recording confession of accused Yon by order dated 6-2-2011, where he noted his age 22 years. In local inspection report of accused Yon (exhibit-26 proved by PW 33) his age was shown 22 years. In the body of the charge sheet as well as in the form of recording statement under section 342 of the Code, his age was shown 21 years. At no point of time, accused Yon claimed him as a child. It appears in the confession of accused Raju that he had passed SSC examination in 2009. In his statement under section 342 of the Code he stated that he had passed SSC in 2010. He did not state his age at the time of passing the examination nor did he submit his school registration or birth certificate to prove his age. In local inspection report (exhibit-27, proved by PW 33) he was shown a youth of 21 years. Both in the charge sheet and form of recording statement under section 342 of the Code, his age shown was 20 years. In such a position, if they did not look like children, the trial Judge had no reason to ascertain their age by further examination. For our satisfaction we have gone through the entire materials including the case diary. We find a photocopy of the passport of accused Nazimuzzaman, where his date of birth was shown 12-12-1989. A ground is taken in the petition of appeal filed by accused Yon, where he was mentioned to be a youth of 17 years. At the material time, child was defined to be a person under the age of 16 years in section 2(f) of the Children Act, 1974. During pendency of the appeal no application for additional evidence or for medical examination of the appellants in order to ascertain their age was moved. At this stage we do not have any reason to hold that at the material time, the appellants were children and their trial was without jurisdiction in view of the provisions of the Children Act.
